haiku-low.q1: No visible difference. Both return 401 'Invalid email or password'. Unknown emails still get a bcrypt compare against a dummy hash and a recorded failure, so timing matches.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 'Too many attempts'. The password is not checked and the attempt is not recorded, so the lock cannot be extended.
haiku-low.q3: If the password matches and the request carried the old sid, the old session row is deleted. A new random session ID is created and set in the cookie.
haiku-low.q4: Only the session ID, no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours since login, even with constant use. The 30-minute idle clock restarts on each request, but the 12-hour absolute limit does not.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the session row if one exists, redirects to /login with 302, and clears the sid cookie with Max-Age=0.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row by sid before responding. If it is already gone, the delete is a no-op and the user still gets 302 to /login with the cookie cleared.
haiku-low.q8: In the shared Postgres database, not process memory. Any instance reads the sessions table using the sid cookie value.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt. The server counts that email's rows with failed_at in the 10 minutes ending now. No stored window start exists.
haiku-low.q10: It checks that the row exists, now minus last_seen_at is at most 30 min, and now minus created_at is at most 12 h. It then sets last_seen_at to now.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 error page with no Set-Cookie header, so the user stays logged out.
haiku-low.q12: The hourly cleanup job. It deletes sessions idle over 30 minutes or older than 12 hours.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get 401 login page with "Invalid email or password". The server still does a bcrypt compare against a dummy hash and records the failure, so timing and lockout behave the same.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked (login_locks.locked_until in the future). The server returns 429 Too many attempts, doesn't check the password and doesn't record the attempt.
sonnet.q3: On a successful login, the old session row is deleted from the sessions table, and a new session ID is generated and inserted.
sonnet.q4: Only the session ID (sid); no user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (created_at), regardless of activity. Idle time stays under 30 min, but the 12 h cap (cookie Max-Age 43200) ends it.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the session row if it exists, then responds 302 to /login and clears the sid cookie (Max-Age=0).
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the session row by sid (a no-op if already gone), then responds 302 to /login and clears sid (Max-Age=0). If storage fails, it returns 503 and leaves the cookie in place.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres sessions table, not in process memory. Any instance reads the row by the sid in the cookie.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt (email lowercase, failed_at), indexed on (email, failed_at). The server counts that email's rows whose failed_at is within the 10 minutes ending now (sliding window, no stored window start).
sonnet.q10: It compares now with last_seen_at (at most 30 min) and with created_at (at most 12 h), and checks that a row exists. When valid, it sets last_seen_at = now, which restarts the idle clock.
sonnet.q11: A 503 error page with no Set-Cookie, so the user stays logged out.
sonnet.q12: The hourly cleanup job, which can run on any instance. It deletes session rows idle over 30 min or older than 12 h. Expired sessions are also deleted when found on a request.
